chapters.1.summary: King Ahaziah of Israel falls through a lattice and is badly hurt. He sends men to ask Baal Zebub, the god of Ekron, if he will recover. Elijah meets them and asks whether Israel has no God. He says the king will die. Ahaziah sends a captain with fifty men to bring Elijah down. Fire from heaven burns them, and then a second fifty. A third captain kneels and begs for his men’s lives. Elijah goes with him, repeats the message, and the king dies.
chapters.1.lds: How does the third captain’s request differ from the first two orders?
chapters.2.summary: Elijah travels from Gilgal to Bethel, Jericho, and the Jordan. Three times he tells Elisha to stay, and Elisha refuses. Elijah strikes the river with his cloak, and they cross on dry ground. Elisha asks for a double share of his spirit. A chariot and horses of fire part them, and Elijah goes up in a whirlwind. Elisha takes up the fallen cloak and parts the Jordan again. He heals Jericho’s bad water with salt. Youths mock him near Bethel, and two bears maul forty-two of them.
chapters.2.lds: The Institute manual connects the mantle with prophetic authority and distinguishes translation from resurrection. What does Elisha ask as he strikes the water (verse 14)?
chapters.3.summary: Jehoram of Israel goes to war when Moab stops paying tribute. Jehoshaphat of Judah and the king of Edom join him. After seven days the armies have no water. Jehoshaphat asks for a prophet, and they find Elisha. Elisha says he helps only for Jehoshaphat’s sake. He promises water without rain, and the valley fills by morning. Moab sees the water red as blood, attacks, and is routed. Moab’s king sacrifices his son on the wall, and Israel withdraws.
chapters.3.lds: The older manual proposes retreat after the heir’s death. It presents the reason as possible. What does Elisha tell Israel’s king to do in verse 13?
chapters.4.summary: A prophet’s widow tells Elisha that a creditor will take her two sons as slaves. She has only a jar of oil. He tells her to borrow empty jars and pour, and the oil fills them all. A wealthy woman of Shunem builds Elisha a room. He promises her a son, and the boy later dies in her lap. She rides to Elisha, and he prays and stretches out on the child. The boy sneezes seven times and opens his eyes. Elisha also cures a poisoned stew and feeds a hundred men.
chapters.4.lds: Come, Follow Me connects Elisha’s care and miracles with Christ’s ministry. What three things does Elisha tell the widow to do in verse 7?
chapters.5.summary: Naaman commands the army of Syria, and he has a skin disease. A captive Israelite girl tells his wife about the prophet in Samaria. Naaman arrives with horses, chariots, and gifts. Elisha sends a messenger: wash seven times in the Jordan. Naaman is angry, but his servants persuade him. He washes and is healed, and he confesses Israel’s God. Elisha refuses any gift. His servant Gehazi runs after Naaman for silver and leaves with the disease.
chapters.5.lds: Come, Follow Me emphasizes humility and receiving help from people with less status. How do Naaman’s servants reason with him in verse 13?
chapters.6.summary: A borrowed axe head falls into the Jordan, and Elisha makes it float. He warns Israel’s king about Syrian ambushes again and again. Syria sends an army to seize him at Dothan. His servant panics until he sees horses and chariots of fire. The Syrians are struck blind, and Elisha leads them into Samaria. He tells the king to feed them and send them home. Later Syria besieges Samaria, and the famine is terrible. The king blames Elisha and swears to kill him.
chapters.6.lds: Come, Follow Me uses the servant’s opened eyes to teach trust in unseen divine help. What does Elisha tell the king to do with the captives (verse 22)?
chapters.7.summary: Elisha says that by tomorrow flour will be cheap at Samaria’s gate. An officer scoffs, and Elisha says he will see it but not eat. Four men with skin disease sit outside the gate. They decide to surrender to the Syrians, since they will die anyway. They find the camp empty, because the LORD made the Syrians hear an army. They eat and hide silver, then decide to report it. The king suspects a trap and sends scouts. The people rush out for food, and the officer is trampled in the gate.
chapters.7.lds: Come, Follow Me invites trust in the fulfillment of God’s word. What do the four men decide in verse 9, and why?
chapters.8.summary: Elisha had warned the woman of Shunem about a seven-year famine. She lived among the Philistines and now returns. She appeals to the king for her house and land. At that moment Gehazi is telling the king about her son. The king restores her property and its income. Elisha goes to Damascus and weeps over what Hazael will do to Israel. Hazael smothers his sick king and takes the throne. In Judah, Jehoram marries Ahab’s daughter and follows Israel’s ways.
chapters.8.lds: What help does the Shunammite need after returning from famine?
chapters.9.summary: Elisha sends a young prophet to anoint Jehu, an army commander, as king. The message is to destroy Ahab’s house. Jehu’s fellow officers blow the trumpet and proclaim him. He drives furiously to Jezreel. King Joram rides out, and Jehu shoots him through the heart. The body is thrown onto Naboth’s field. Jehu’s men also kill Ahaziah king of Judah. Jezebel is thrown from a window, and dogs eat her body.
chapters.9.lds: The older manual distinguishes a predicted political outcome from approval of Jehu’s methods. Whose blood does verse 26 say the LORD has seen?
chapters.10.summary: Jehu writes to Samaria’s leaders, and they send him the heads of Ahab’s seventy sons. He kills all who remain of Ahab’s house in Jezreel. He also kills forty-two relatives of Judah’s king. He invites Jehonadab to see his zeal for the LORD. By a trick he gathers Baal’s worshipers into their temple and kills them. He destroys the temple and makes it a latrine. Yet he keeps Jeroboam’s golden calves. Hazael of Syria begins to take Israel’s land east of the Jordan.
chapters.10.lds: The older Church manual questions Jehu's motives. What does verse 31 say Jehu did not do?
chapters.11.summary: Athaliah, mother of the dead king of Judah, kills the royal children and rules. The king’s sister Jehosheba steals away the baby Joash. He is hidden in the temple for six years. In the seventh year the priest Jehoiada brings in the guard captains. They surround the boy, crown him, and give him the covenant. Athaliah hears the noise and cries, “Treason!” She is put to death outside the temple. The people tear down Baal’s temple, and Joash takes the throne at seven.
chapters.11.lds: The older manual emphasizes the child’s protection and Jehoiada’s guidance. Where is the child kept for six years (verse 3)?
chapters.12.summary: Joash does right as long as the priest Jehoiada teaches him. He tells the priests to use offerings to repair the temple. After many years no repairs are done. Jehoiada sets a chest with a hole in its lid beside the altar. The king’s scribe and the high priest count the silver. It is paid straight to carpenters, masons, and stonecutters. Later Hazael threatens Jerusalem, and Joash buys him off with temple treasure. His own servants kill him.
chapters.12.lds: The older manual studies the collection system and Jehoiada’s support. Who was not asked to give an account in verse 15?
chapters.13.summary: Jehoahaz rules Israel, and Hazael of Syria crushes his army. He seeks the LORD, and Israel gets relief. His son Jehoash visits the dying Elisha and weeps over him. Elisha has him shoot an arrow east and calls it the LORD’s arrow of victory. He tells him to strike the ground with the other arrows. The king strikes three times and stops, and Elisha is angry. Elisha dies, and a dead man revives on touching his bones. Jehoash defeats Syria three times.
chapters.13.lds: The older manual connects Elisha’s arrows with victories over Syria. Why is Elisha angry in verse 19?
chapters.14.summary: Amaziah of Judah executes the servants who killed his father. He spares their children, as the law of Moses requires. He defeats Edom and then challenges Jehoash of Israel. Jehoash answers with a fable of a thistle and a cedar. Judah is beaten, Jerusalem’s wall is broken, and the temple gold is taken. Amaziah is later killed at Lachish. In Israel, Jeroboam the second rules forty-one years and does evil. Yet he restores Israel’s borders, as the prophet Jonah had said.
chapters.14.lds: The older manual studies Amaziah’s divided commitment and his failure to heed warning. What law does verse 6 quote?
chapters.15.summary: Azariah rules Judah fifty-two years and lives apart with a skin disease. In Israel, Zechariah rules six months and is murdered. Shallum lasts one month before Menahem kills him. Menahem pays the king of Assyria a thousand talents of silver to keep his throne. His son Pekahiah is killed by Pekah, an officer. Tiglath Pileser of Assyria takes Galilee and Gilead and deports the people. Hoshea kills Pekah and rules. In Judah, Jotham does right, but the high places remain.
chapters.15.lds: The older manual connects Uzziah’s account in Chronicles with respect for priesthood authority. Who pays the money in verse 20?
chapters.16.summary: Ahaz rules Judah and does not do right. He even burns his son as an offering. The kings of Syria and Israel attack Jerusalem. Ahaz sends temple silver to Tiglath Pileser and calls himself his servant and son. Assyria captures Damascus. Ahaz goes there, sees an altar, and sends its design to the priest Urijah. Urijah builds a copy, and the king offers on it. Ahaz moves the bronze altar and strips other temple furnishings because of Assyria’s king.
chapters.16.lds: How does Ahaz’s need for foreign help change temple worship?
chapters.17.summary: Hoshea of Israel stops paying Assyria and looks to Egypt. Assyria jails him and besieges Samaria for three years. The city falls, and Israel is carried away to Assyria. The writer explains that Israel served other gods and ignored every prophet. Judah also failed to keep the commandments. Assyria settles people from other lands in Samaria’s towns. Lions attack them, and a priest is sent back to teach about the LORD. They fear the LORD and also serve their own gods.
chapters.17.lds: The older manual applies the fall to the need to heed prophetic warnings. Whom does Assyria settle in Samaria’s towns (verse 24)?
chapters.18.summary: Hezekiah rules Judah and trusts the LORD more than any king before him. He removes the high places and breaks Moses’s bronze serpent, which people worshiped. He rebels against Assyria. Samaria falls in his sixth year. In his fourteenth year Sennacherib takes Judah’s walled towns. Hezekiah sends tribute and strips gold from the temple doors. Assyria still sends an army and a spokesman to Jerusalem. He shouts in Hebrew that no god has saved any land from Assyria.
chapters.18.lds: Come, Follow Me studies Hezekiah’s trust during threats. What does Hezekiah say to the king of Assyria in verse 14?
chapters.19.summary: Hezekiah tears his clothes and sends to the prophet Isaiah. Isaiah says not to fear the Assyrian’s words. The spokesman rejoins his king, who has left Lachish for Libnah. Sennacherib sends a letter mocking the LORD. Hezekiah spreads the letter out in the temple and prays. Isaiah answers that Assyria’s king will not enter the city or shoot an arrow there. That night the LORD’s angel strikes the Assyrian camp. Sennacherib goes home to Nineveh, where his sons kill him.
chapters.19.lds: Come, Follow Me encourages prayer and trust when facing severe difficulties. What does Hezekiah do with the letter in verse 14?
chapters.20.summary: Hezekiah falls sick, and Isaiah tells him he will die. He turns to the wall, prays, and weeps. Before Isaiah leaves the palace, the LORD sends him back. Hezekiah will live fifteen more years, and the city will be saved. As a sign the shadow moves back ten steps. Envoys come from the king of Babylon with letters and a gift. Hezekiah shows them all his treasures and weapons. Isaiah says all of it, and some of his sons, will go to Babylon.
chapters.20.lds: The older manual connects Hezekiah’s prayer with trust in divine care. What does verse 17 say will be left?
chapters.21.summary: Manasseh becomes king at twelve and rules fifty-five years. He rebuilds the high places his father Hezekiah destroyed. He sets up altars for Baal and for the stars inside the temple courts. He burns his son as an offering and uses sorcery. The prophets say Jerusalem will be wiped like a dish. Manasseh also sheds much innocent blood. His son Amon rules two years and is killed by his servants. The people make Amon’s son Josiah king.
chapters.21.lds: Manasseh reverses many of Hezekiah's changes. How do a leader's choices affect other people?
chapters.22.summary: Josiah becomes king at eight and does what is right. In his eighteenth year he orders repairs to the temple. The high priest Hilkiah finds the book of the law there. The scribe Shaphan reads it to the king, and Josiah tears his clothes. He sends five officials to ask the LORD about it. They go to the prophetess Huldah in Jerusalem. She says the book’s disaster will come on the city. Because Josiah humbled himself, he will not see it.
chapters.22.lds: Come, Follow Me connects scripture with changes of heart and commitment. To whom do the king’s officials go in verse 14?
chapters.23.summary: Josiah reads the book of the covenant to all the people and renews the covenant. He removes Baal’s vessels and the Asherah pole from the temple. He defiles the high places from Geba to Beersheba. He destroys the altar at Bethel, as a man of God had foretold. He orders a Passover such as had not been kept since the judges. No king before him turned to the LORD as he did. Still the LORD’s anger against Judah remains. Pharaoh Necoh kills Josiah at Megiddo, and Egypt chooses the next king.
chapters.23.lds: Come, Follow Me studies Josiah’s promise to God. Which actions follow his reading of the law?
chapters.24.summary: Jehoiakim serves Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon for three years and then rebels. Raiders attack Judah, as the prophets had said. His son Jehoiachin rules three months. Nebuchadnezzar besieges Jerusalem, and the young king surrenders. Babylon takes the treasures of the temple and palace. Ten thousand people go into exile, including the king and his mother. Only the poorest remain in the land. Babylon makes Zedekiah king, and he too rebels.
chapters.24.lds: The older manual connects Zedekiah’s setting with Lehi in the Book of Mormon. This is an LDS cross-reference. Which groups does verse 14 say were taken away?
chapters.25.summary: Nebuchadnezzar besieges Jerusalem for about two years, and famine grips the city. The wall is breached, and Zedekiah flees by night. He is caught, his sons are killed before him, and he is blinded. A month later the Babylonians burn the temple, the palace, and the houses. They break down the walls and carry off the bronze. Gedaliah is made governor and is soon murdered. The remaining people flee to Egypt. Years later Babylon’s new king frees Jehoiachin and feeds him at his table.
chapters.25.lds: What changes when Jehoiachin receives kindness at the end of the book?
